kurz: How subsidised private retirement provision works from 2027: contract types, allowances, permitted investments, the standard account with its cost cap, the payout and the way out of a Riester contract.

bloecke.md:
The Retirement Provision Reform Act (Altersvorsorgereformgesetz) of 26 May 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I no. 156, promulgated on 29 May 2026) reorganises subsidised private retirement provision. The core rules apply from 1 January 2027. From that day, contracts under the old Riester rules may no longer be sold (Section 14(7) AltZertG in the new version). Existing contracts continue.

In the law, the new contracts are still called retirement provision contracts (Altersvorsorgevertrag). There are three forms for the accumulation phase. A guarantee product promises 80% or 100% of contributions including allowances at the start of the pension. The retirement investment account (Altersvorsorgedepot) has no guarantee, and the standard account contract (Standarddepot-Vertrag Altersvorsorge) is a special form of it with capped costs. Home ownership contracts for loans and building savings continue alongside them. The information in this lesson reflects the situation on 15 October 2026.

bloecke.md:
## Who is eligible

The existing groups remain eligible: compulsorily insured members of the statutory pension insurance, civil servants, judges and soldiers who consent to the transfer of data, and some equivalent groups such as those insured under the farmers' old-age security scheme (Alterssicherung der Landwirte). Two new groups are added (Section 10a(1) sentence 5 EStG in the new version). These are self-employed people under 67 with income from a business or from self-employed work who file a tax return for the contribution year, and employees who pay contributions as compulsory members of a professional pension scheme (berufsständisches Versorgungswerk), for example doctors, lawyers or architects.

A spouse without an entitlement of their own is indirectly eligible if the spouses do not live permanently apart, the spouse has a contract of their own and personally pays in at least €120 a year. Their basic allowance is at most €175. Per person, at most two contracts concluded after 31 December 2026 are subsidised (Section 82(5) EStG in the new version).

## Allowances and tax deduction

From 2027, the subsidy depends directly on your own contribution. The basic allowance is 50 cents per euro paid in up to €360 and 25 cents per further euro up to €1,800, together at most €540 (Section 84 EStG in the new version). For each child for whom the saver receives child benefit (Kindergeld), a child allowance of one euro per euro paid in is added, at most €300 (Section 85 EStG). Anyone who is younger than 25 at the start of the contribution year receives a one-off career starter bonus of €200.

Allowances are only paid with an own contribution of at least €120 a year (Section 86 EStG in the new version). The old calculation based on 4% of the previous year's income no longer applies. Up to €6,840 a year may be paid in, of which at most €1,800 is subsidised.

bloecke.erklaerung: B is your own annual contribution. Below €120 there is no allowance. According to the wording of the law, the child allowance is calculated separately for each child from the same contribution: min(B, €300).

bloecke.beispiel: With an own contribution of €1,200, the result is 50% × €360 = €180 and 25% × €840 = €210, together a basic allowance of €390. That is 32.5% of the own contribution.

bloecke.titel: Tax deduction with the most-favourable assessment
bloecke.md: Contributions of up to €1,800 plus the allowances are deductible as special expenses (Section 10a(1) EStG in the new version). The tax office checks whether the tax saving is higher than the allowances and refunds only the difference ([[Most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung)|most-favourable assessment (Günstigerprüfung)]]). An approximation with a 30% [[Marginal tax rate|marginal tax rate]], without solidarity surcharge and church tax: with a contribution of €1,800 and no children, (€1,800 + €540) × 30% gives a saving of €702. That is €162 above the allowance, which raises the subsidy to 39% of the own contribution. With two children, the allowances of €1,140 exceed the saving of €882, and the allowances alone apply.

## What the account may hold

The law lists the permitted investments exhaustively (Section 1(1b) AltZertG in the new version):

- investment funds under the EU directive for [[UCITS (OGAW)|UCITS]], including most ETFs, with a key information document and at most risk class 5 of 7
- open-ended retail funds set up as mixed or other investment funds, also up to risk class 5
- open-ended European long-term investment funds (ELTIF) up to risk class 5
- euro bonds of the federal government, the federal states and municipalities, of euro area states, the EU, the European Investment Bank and the EFSF

The risk class is the [[Summary risk indicator (SRI)|summary risk indicator (SRI)]] from the key information document. Individual shares, corporate bonds, crypto assets and funds in classes 6 and 7 are excluded. The provider selects the investments. The contract may allow the saver to choose from the range offered. For the free retirement investment account, the law contains no obligation to shift into safer investments before the pension starts.

## The standard account

Every provider of a guarantee product or retirement investment account must offer at least one standard account contract, either itself or through a partner (Section 1(3) AltZertG in the new version). It must be possible to conclude the contract online. The provider selects two UCITS funds, a cautious one in risk class 1 or 2 and a riskier one in class 3, 4 or 5. The saver decides how contributions and allowances are split between the two funds. If the saver makes no decision, the split that the contract provides for this case applies. There is no statutory default ratio.

Before the pension starts, the provider shifts the money along a fixed path. Five years before the payout begins, at most 50% may be held in the riskier fund, and from two years before, at most 30%. The saver can request different shares.

bloecke.titel: Maximum share of the riskier fund in the standard account
bloecke.unter: Under Section 1(1c) no. 5 AltZertG in the new version. Until five years before the start, only the split chosen by the saver applies; the value 100 stands for the absence of a statutory limit.
kategorien: more than 5 years before the start

bloecke.md: The [[Reduction in yield (Effektivkosten)|reduction in yield (Effektivkosten)]] of the standard account may be at most 1.0% (Section 2a(2) AltZertG in the new version). The government draft of February 2026 still provided for 1.5%. What is measured is the reduction in return caused by all costs up to the start of the payout, calculated like the summary cost indicator of the European PRIIPs Regulation. The cap therefore limits the average annual reduction in yield and is no deduction from contributions. An auditor or actuary must confirm compliance at least every three years. No cap applies to the free retirement investment account or to guarantee products. There, only a comparison of the reduction in yield in the product information sheet helps.

- The federal government may designate a public body for a state standard account by ordinance (Section 1(1e) AltZertG in the new version). By mid-October 2026 this ordinance had not been issued, and press reports consider a start on 1 January 2027 unlikely.
- Which funds and which default split providers choose for the standard account will only be shown by the model product information, which must be published before sales begin.
- Costs announced by individual providers are advertising statements. The binding document is the individual product information sheet.

## Payout

For new contracts, the payout begins at age 65 at the earliest, and earlier only if a statutory old-age pension begins before then. It must begin at age 70 at the latest, and without an agreement it begins at 65 (Section 1(1) sentence 1 no. 2 and Section 7b AltZertG in the new version). With the retirement investment account, the saver chooses the start within a window of at least five years and gives notice at least three months beforehand. At the start, up to 30% of the capital can be paid out at once. For the rest there are three forms.

bloecke.md: Under the old Riester rules, part of the capital in a withdrawal plan had to be converted into an annuity from age 85. This obligation no longer applies to new contracts. Cover for reduced earning capacity and for surviving dependants can no longer be agreed in new contracts; only an [[Annuity guarantee period (Rentengarantiezeit)|annuity guarantee period (Rentengarantiezeit)]] is permitted. The provider may settle very small pensions of up to 1.5% of the monthly reference value (Bezugsgröße), about €59 a month in 2026, with a one-off payment.

## Taxes and harmful use

In the accumulation phase, income within the contract is not taxed. Payouts are other income under Section 22 no. 5 EStG. To the extent that they are based on subsidised contributions, allowances and the income earned on them, they are taxed in full at the personal tax rate ([[Deferred taxation (nachgelagerte Besteuerung)|deferred taxation]]). Contributions above €1,800 are not subsidised. For their share, only the income portion (Ertragsanteil) is taxed with a lifelong pension, and with payouts from an account the difference between the payout and the contributions paid in.

Anyone who has subsidised capital paid out other than in the permitted forms uses it harmfully (schädliche Verwendung, Section 93 EStG). The allowances and the separately determined tax advantages must then be repaid, and the income is taxed. This also applies to termination without a transfer and to payment to heirs. The following are not harmful use: a transfer to another retirement provision contract of your own, a transfer to the contract of the surviving spouse if both did not live permanently apart and lived in the EU or the EEA, payments from an annuity guarantee period and the settlement of a small pension.

## Changing provider and cost information

A contract can be made dormant or terminated with three months' notice to the end of a quarter in order to transfer the capital to another contract of your own. For contracts under the new rules, the previous provider may charge at most €150 for this in the first five years. After that, switching is free, as it is after a cost increase. The new provider may not charge acquisition and distribution costs on transferred subsidised capital, only a one-off administration fee of up to €150 (Section 1(1) sentences 3 and 4 AltZertG in the new version). Under the old rules, acquisition costs could still be charged on up to 50% of the transferred capital.

Before concluding the contract, the saver receives an individual product information sheet with the reduction in yield, risk class, scenarios and the consequences of a switch. Every year there follows information on capital, income and the actual costs of the previous year. The provider must announce cost increases four months in advance to the end of a quarter.

## Existing Riester contracts

Contracts concluded before 1 January 2027 keep their terms and the old subsidy until the pension starts: a basic allowance of €175, €185 or €300 per child and a minimum own contribution of 4% of the previous year's gross income less the allowances, at least €60 (Section 52(50a) EStG in the new version). Two routes lead into the new subsidy rules.

1. An irrevocable declaration to the provider. It applies to all of your own old contracts at once and from the contribution year in which it is received.
2. Concluding a new contract from 2027. The new rules then apply automatically to all contracts of that person.

From 2027, the capital of an old contract can be transferred to a retirement investment account without losing the subsidy. To do so, the old contract is terminated with three months' notice to the end of a quarter, and the previous provider may charge up to €150 under the old terms. The contribution guarantee of a Riester contract applies at the start of the payout. Anyone who transfers earlier takes the current balance along, and the guarantee stays behind.

**Single parent, two children born 2008 or later, previous year's gross income €15,000.** Under the old rules, 4% of income comes to €600. After deducting allowances of €775, nothing remains, so the base amount of €60 applies. An own contribution of €60 brings in €775 in allowances. Under the new rules, an own contribution of €300 is needed for €750 in allowances, namely a basic allowance of €150 and twice a child allowance of €300.

**Single, no children, previous year's gross income €40,000.** Under the old rules, an own contribution of €1,425 is needed for an allowance of €175. Under the new rules, the same €1,425 brings a basic allowance of €446.25, and €1,800 brings €540.

The old rules are more favourable for the first household, the new rules for the second. Because a single new contract moves all contracts to the new rules, it pays to do the calculation under both versions before any new contract.

bloecke.titel: Early start pension, as of 15 October 2026
bloecke.md: The planned early start pension (Frühstart-Rente) builds on the retirement investment account. Under the government draft, the federal government pays €10 a month for every child resident in Germany from the 6th to the 18th birthday into a retirement investment account contract of the child, to which the rules of the standard account apply. Without a contract, the money is to be invested in a special federal fund. The Finance Committee of the Bundestag approved it on 14 October 2026. The vote in the Bundestag is planned for 16 October, after which the Bundesrat must consent. The law has therefore not yet been passed, and details may change.

- Compare the reduction in yield in the individual product information sheet. For the standard account it is at most 1.0%; for other accounts and guarantee products it can be considerably higher.
- Pay in €1,800 a year for the full basic allowance and at least €300 for the full child allowance. Below €120 there is no allowance.
- With an existing Riester contract, work out the allowances under the old and the new rules before concluding a new contract or making the declaration. Neither step can be undone, and both apply to all contracts.
- The money is tied up until at least 65. For earlier goals, a free securities account is better suited.
- A switch costs up to €150 in the first five years and nothing after that.

The retirement investment account subsidises the first €360 of annual contributions at 50% and further contributions up to €1,800 at 25%, plus up to €300 per child. For the first time, subsidised money may be held in funds and ETFs without a guarantee. Whether it pays off depends on the reduction in yield, the lock-in until 65 and the tax rate in old age.

mitnehmen: From 2027 there are guarantee products with an 80% or 100% guarantee, the retirement investment account without a guarantee and the standard account with a reduction in yield of at most 1.0%; Riester contracts are no longer sold.
The basic allowance is 50% of the first €360 and 25% up to €1,800, at most €540; up to €300 per child is added, provided the own contribution is at least €120.
The account may only hold funds and ETFs up to risk class 5 and euro bonds of public issuers; individual shares are excluded.
Payouts start from 65 and at the latest from 70, with up to 30% as a lump sum and as a life annuity or withdrawal plan until at least 85; subsidised benefits are taxed in full.

Old Riester contracts keep their subsidy; a new contract from 2027 or the switching declaration irrevocably moves all contracts to the new rules, which can be unfavourable for low earners with children.

begriffe.text: Statutory form of the retirement investment account from 2027 (Section 1(1c) AltZertG). The provider selects two funds, a cautious one in risk class 1 or 2 and a riskier one in classes 3 to 5, shifts the money before the pension starts and may charge a reduction in yield of at most 1.0%. Every provider of subsidised contracts must offer it.

Payout of subsidised retirement capital outside the permitted forms, for example on termination without a transfer or on payment to heirs (Section 93 EStG). The allowances and tax advantages must then be repaid, and the income is taxed.

Subsidised retirement provision contract concluded before 1 January 2027. It keeps the old Riester subsidy until the pension starts, as long as the saver does not switch to the new rules by declaration or by concluding a new contract.

One-off payout of up to 30% of the capital available at the start of the pension from a subsidised retirement provision contract. It is not harmful use and is taxed like the other benefits under Section 22 no. 5 EStG.
